title: 7 Small, Simple Classroom Management Resolutions For 2023
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin frames improved classroom management as achievable through small, low-effort adjustments rather than strain, and offers seven resolutions requiring only commitment, not extra planning. They include eliminating all friction with students during consequences, fully trusting a classroom management plan rather than relying on perfect words in the moment, shifting responsibility for listening and behaving entirely onto students, cultivating calm as a deliberate daily decision, holding no grudges as the real secret to rapport, setting students up for success through detailed instruction of every transition, and adopting a mindset that accepts only excellence. He closes by urging readers to commit fully and get back on track quickly after any lapse, framing sustained commitment to these seven small shifts as producing outsized transformation in a classroom.
points: Improved classroom management should be a small, low-effort shift, not extra work — 'if it feels hard... you're doing it wrong.'
Resolution One: eliminate all friction with students, staying purely pleasant even while enforcing consequences.
Resolution Two: fully trust the classroom management plan rather than relying on the perfect words in the moment.
Resolution Five: hold no grudges, framed as the real secret to building rapport, rather than getting to know students personally.
Resolution Seven: adopt a mindset that accepts only excellence, since students calibrate to the standard a teacher visibly expects.
quotes: If it feels hard, if you’re straining and striving but reaping little more than stress, then you’re doing it wrong.
Stop all friction with students. Resolve to never lecture, scold, or show an ounce of displeasure.

Let your classroom management plan do all the work for you. Relieve yourself of the profound distress of having to rely on the perfect, unattainable alchemy of words and expressions to curb misbehavior.
Hold no grudge. The secret to influential rapport isn’t to try to get to know your students better.
Accept only excellence. This is a mindset, not a task. If your attitude is one of expecting the best, finest, and highest quality, then that’s what you’ll get it.
